chapter_theme: The invocation (காப்பு) of Subramaniar Njanam, which compresses the whole work into one stanza: subsiding in the unceasing suzhumunai, going by the vaasi into Siva-yoga, knowing the way, taking silence, climbing to the summit of the cosmic bound, taking the vel of Om, seeing oneself by the clarified mind, dwelling in the supreme void and becoming the Shakti-Siva of Vedanta. Murugan's vel is already the pranava, and his ascent is the breath's.

2485.reading: Subsiding in the unceasing suzhumunai, going by the vaasi of the kala that has come into Siva-yoga, knowing the way and the ford, taking silence, going up to the great summit of the cosmic bound, taking the clear vel that is the shape of Om, seeing oneself by the clarified mind's knowledge, dwelling in the open supreme space and becoming the Shakti-Siva of Vedanta: this is the guard.
2485.nuance: A kaappu normally invokes a god; this one invokes a practice, and Murugan appears only as his vel, which is named the shape of Om. The work's closing verse (2517) returns to the same summit and the same Om-vel, so the invocation is also its summary. The stanza's lines are unevenly divided in the source.

links.note: Thiruvalluvar Njanam's invocation hails Guhan (Murugan) seated within the kundalini and the lotus of the suzhumunai; here the suzhumunai is the place where the practice subsides and Murugan is present as the Om-vel. In both, Murugan is a resident of the central channel.

Tirumular says what the masters attain is two things, Omkara and the five letters; the invocation makes Om, in the shape of the vel, the instrument by which one sees oneself and reaches the supreme void.

new_concepts.gloss: the central channel (sushumna) of the yogic body, between the left and right channels, in which the breath is made to rise
the breath as the Siddhars' practice: the in- and out-breath, coded as the sun and moon and as the horse, whose mastery is the way to siddhi

source_issues: 2485: the eight lines are printed with uneven breaks (line 3 and line 5 each carry part of the next line), so the metrical division is lost.
